summary: 25 unit tests across three logical groups (vocabulary / build_admin_ping / sanitize_error_message). All tests pass. Good isolation via monkeypatch; explicit test-method names; byte-for-byte equality on ping format; edge cases for empty/whitespace/unset env, unicode exception, BadExc.__str__ raising. One missing edge case around pre-existing [REDACTED] markers — minor, doesn't block.

findings.finding: No test covers the case where the raw exception string itself already contains `[REDACTED]` (e.g. upstream library already redacted something, or operator pasted the marker in a message). The count assertion `result.count('[REDACTED]') == 4` in test_sanitize_redacts_all_four_in_one_string would be sensitive to this pre-existing marker. Low impact in practice.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add `test_sanitize_preserves_preexisting_redacted_marker` verifying behaviour. Task-3 Acceptance doesn't require it. No action.

findings.finding: `test_ignores_unknown_source_name` and `test_multiple_unknowns_still_counted_in_prefix` correctly verify the edge case from task-3 spec (N in prefix = len(rows) including 'other'). Good alignment with spec's strict N-vs-counter-sum distinction.

Test file imports `SOURCE_EMOJI`, `SOURCE_LABEL`, `build_admin_ping`, `sanitize_error_message` at module load. If any of those is missing, pytest collection fails loudly rather than reporting N individual failures. This is the desired behaviour for a foundational module — fail early.
`clean_secret_env` fixture yields the monkeypatch object directly; tests call `.setenv(...)` on the yielded object. Idiomatic pytest, clear, no confusion. Good.
Explicit `BadExc` class whose `__str__` raises proves the outer try/except works. This is the strongest test in the suite for the 'sanitizer must not break caller' contract.
findings.recommendation: No action — excellent coverage of the graceful-degradation requirement.
